citations.cite: Cal. Supreme Court No. S275431 (Cal. Mar. 25, 2024)
citations.quote: First, an employee’s time spent on an employer’s premises awaiting and undergoing an employer-mandated exit procedure that includes the employer’s visual inspection of the employee’s personal vehicle is compensable as “hours worked” within the meaning of Wage Order No. 16, section 2(J).

citations.cite: Cal. Supreme Court No. S275431 (Cal. Mar. 25, 2024)
citations.quote: Separately, this travel time is not compensable as “hours worked” because an employer’s imposition of ordinary workplace rules on employees during their drive to the worksite in a personal vehicle does not create the requisite level of employer control.

citations.cite: Cal. Supreme Court No. S275431 (Cal. Mar. 25, 2024)
citations.quote: Second, the time that an employee spends traveling between the Security Gate and the employee parking lots is compensable as “employer-mandated travel” under Wage Order No. 16, section 5(A)
